title: 3Sum
keyIdea: Sort. Fix nums[i] (skipping repeated values), then run two pointers j = i + 1, k = n − 1 on the rest: sum < 0 → j++, > 0 → k−−, = 0 → record and move both, skipping equal neighbours so no triplet repeats. O(n²).

approaches.name: Brute force: all triples + set
approaches.idea: Try every i < j < k; sort each zero-sum triple and keep it in a set to remove repeats.
approaches.why: n³/6 triples; the set insert adds a log factor.

approaches.name: Sort + two pointers
approaches.idea: Sort; for each new value nums[i], two pointers find pairs summing to −nums[i]; skip duplicates for i, j and k.
approaches.why: n values of i × an O(n) sweep each; sorting is O(n log n).

options: Two pointers need order, and equal values end up side by side for easy skipping

quiz.q: Why skip i when nums[i] == nums[i − 1]?
options: The same first number would find the same triplets again
It can't be part of a triplet

quiz.q: After recording a triplet, why move BOTH j and k?
options: With nums[i] fixed, changing only one side can't give zero again with the same other value
